subject.title: Allow before_agent_start hooks to override prompt

question: Should an installed plugin with prompt-injection permission be allowed to replace the current user prompt, and if so should the highest-priority plugin win while preserving separate provenance for the original user input?
rationale: The capability is technically feasible and vision-aligned, but it expands a public plugin security boundary and cannot be implemented safely without intentional precedence, provenance, and audit semantics.

options.title: Add gated replacement
options.body: Add one prompt replacement result to `before_prompt_build`, inherit it through the legacy hook, use higher-priority-first precedence, preserve original-input provenance separately, and enforce `allowPromptInjection`.

options.title: Keep additive hooks only
options.body: Reject replacement and retain additive context plus `before_agent_run` blocking as the supported plugin boundary.

recommendation.title: Add gated replacement
recommendation.body: Add one prompt replacement result to `before_prompt_build`, inherit it through the legacy hook, use higher-priority-first precedence, preserve original-input provenance separately, and enforce `allowPromptInjection`.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced Codex prompt-hook parity and own much of the recent shared-harness prompt-range and effective-input history needed for this decision.
